title: The Girl at the Closed Gate

dialogue.text: The first morning of the new school term -- and Aoi is already running late.
No, no, no -- not on the very first day!
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: exasperated

dialogue.text: Aoi skids around the corner of her street, one sock still slouching at her ankle, her school bag thumping against her side.
Stupid alarm, why did you die today of all days?!
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: exasperated

dialogue.text: She had set three alarms. All three screens had gone black in the night, drained at once for no reason she could explain.
Mom's going to say it was fate punishing me for scrolling at midnight...
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: exasperated

dialogue.text: At the shortcut behind the shopping street, she slows.
The old service gate to the school wall is standing open.
Wait, seriously? They never open this gate.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: astonished

dialogue.text: A girl in the same uniform stands beside it, pale in the morning light, holding the bars with both hands.
If you go through the front, you'll be late.
dialogue.speaker: Girl

dialogue.text: Yeah, that was the problem, thanks.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: exasperated

dialogue.text: Take this way instead. And don't use the east stairs today.
dialogue.speaker: Girl

dialogue.text: ...That's weirdly specific.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: uneasy_confused

dialogue.text: The girl looks at Aoi's chest, at the ribbon she'd tied in a rushed, crooked knot.
You always pull the left side tighter when you're nervous.
dialogue.speaker: Girl

dialogue.text: "Always"? We've never met.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: astonished

dialogue.text: A chill runs under Aoi's collar despite the warm spring air.
Hurry. You're in Class 1-C now.
dialogue.speaker: Girl

dialogue.text: How do you know that before the board goes up?
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: astonished

dialogue.text: The girl doesn't answer. She presses something into Aoi's hand — a small brass key on a faded blue string.
You'll need it later.
dialogue.speaker: Girl

dialogue.text: Aoi stares for half a beat, then laughs once out of pure nerves.
Okay, wow. Creepy. Helpful, maybe, but creepy.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: uneasy_confused

dialogue.text: She darts through the gate anyway.
The shortcut spits her out beside the gym, shaving precious minutes off the trip.
Yes! I might actually make it!
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: natural_smile_cheerful

dialogue.text: A crash splits the air from inside the main building.
Students near the entrance gasp and recoil as a maintenance cart lies tipped across the bottom of the east stairwell, mops and buckets scattered everywhere.
Good thing nobody was on the stairs.
dialogue.speaker: Male Student

dialogue.text: Aoi stops cold, breath caught halfway in.
No way...
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: astonished

dialogue.text: Her fingers tighten around the brass key until the edges bite into her palm.
She said not to use the east stairs.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: uneasy_confused

dialogue.text: Heart hammering now for a totally different reason, Aoi spins and looks back toward the service gate.
It is closed.
Locked, chained, and dusty, as if it has not been opened in months.
Oh, come on. Don't do this to me on day one.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: exasperated

dialogue.text: A teacher starts herding students away from the stairwell, and the tide of bodies pulls Aoi toward the shoe lockers.
Fine. School first. Panic attack later.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: exasperated

dialogue.text: She slips the blue string into her blazer pocket and hurries inside, unable to shake the feeling that the morning has only just begun.
